primary_source.title: Does Verbal Self-Reflection Transfer to Long-Horizon Scientific Discovery?

verified_results: The paper compares BASE against REFLEXION on the same 30 chemical systems per model, eight episodes per system and oracle budget B=40. It states that all other hyperparameters, tools and prompts are held fixed between conditions.
Headline per-episode stable discoveries are Qwen3-30B BASE 9.82 versus REFLEXION 14.43 and Qwen3.5-122B BASE 14.82 versus REFLEXION 21.28, with reported Wilcoxon p<1e-4 for both model contrasts.

Cross-episode fitted slopes are -0.24 versus +0.72 for Qwen3-30B and -0.04 versus +1.26 for Qwen3.5-122B. The environment state is reset each episode and the reflection memory is the designed cross-episode information channel.
Breadth decreases under REFLEXION: unique compositions per episode 9.18 to 5.14 for 30B and 20.90 to 18.95 for 122B; space-group entropy and mean sampled hull distance also decrease.
The paper explicitly says the predicted counterproductive effect on sparser search spaces is not directly tested.

Manual qualitative inspection of Qwen3.5-122B REFLEXION runs reports recurring actor non-compliance with query caps, mandated element exclusions and already-stable-composition avoidance. The paper explicitly recommends moving repeatedly unenforced constraints into the environment or tool schema.

scope_corrections.correction: Treat the matched intervention as the REFLEXION package, not an isolated memory-storage component. REFLEXION adds a reflector call, generated reflection content, persistent memory and prompt injection together. The actor and reflector use the same underlying LLM, and the paper itself lists a fixed-reflector controlled study as future work. Therefore the observed gain is strong within-benchmark evidence for the bundled episodic-reflection mechanism, but it does not isolate storage/memory from extra reflective computation or reflection quality.

The detailed recurring non-compliance analysis in Section 5.2 is stated to come from manual inspection of Qwen3.5-122B under REFLEXION. Do not automatically promote that qualitative failure prevalence to Qwen3-30B, other model families, or scientific agents generally.

A machine-enforceable constraint actuator was not experimentally tested. The source itself motivates essentially this design direction by recommending query caps/coverage constraints be moved into the environment or tool schema. Candidate 042's controller implementation remains an untested extension, not an experimentally demonstrated repair.
The paper observes breadth collapse in tested MADE systems but explicitly labels failure on sparser spaces as a falsifiable prediction that was not tested.

The paper reports Wilcoxon p-values and system-level slope signs, but the retrieved paper text does not specify random seed control, repeated independent replicate campaigns, or a separate variance-component analysis. Do not reinterpret the p-values as proving robustness across independent stochastic reruns beyond the reported experimental panel.

assessment: Candidate 042 has a well-supported motivation: a matched BASE-vs-REFLEXION condition contrast improves yield while reducing breadth, and qualitative evidence shows some verbal constraints are ignored. The proposed hard actuator is plausible and directly aligned with the authors' own stated practical implication, but it remains untested. Preserve the distinction between evidence for bundled REFLEXION, observed breadth/non-compliance, and the untested actuator repair.
exact_next_action: Rotate to another under-audited C14 namespace and prioritize a source-qualified quantitative or authority-boundary claim with primary/raw artifacts; do not repeat the already-audited Darwin or Argus C14 claims.
